channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Regulate Online Personal Fundraising
item.description: Kazakhstan is proposing new rules to regulate personal online fundraising. Citizens collecting money for personal needs will be required to report on how donations are spent. The Ministry of Culture and Information published the draft project. Violators face administrative or criminal liability. This also includes changes for charitable organizations.

item.title: Kazakhstan Experts Advise Locking In Deposit Rates Amid Expected National Bank Rate Cut
item.description: A Kazakhstani financier predicts the National Bank will lower its base rate on October 23rd, potentially more than anticipated. He advises citizens to secure current deposit rates, which are around 18-19% annually, before potential changes. Inflation slowdown and a stronger tenge are cited as reasons for the expected cut.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Prime Minister Discusses Joint Projects with Foreign Investors at Investment Roundtable
item.description: Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov met with leaders from Aksa Energy, Carlsberg Kazakhstan, Solico Group, and CONTEC at the IX Kazakhstan Global Investment Roundtable in Shymkent. Discussions focused on expanding cooperation in energy, food, agro-industrial, and space sectors, emphasizing localization and new technologies. Projects in energy and food production were highlighted.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan Poised to Attract More Western Banks, According to Raiffeisen
item.description: Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan show strong potential for attracting Western banks, which are increasingly interested in Central Asia and the Caucasus. Raiffeisen Research notes that while foreign financial institutions' presence is currently small, growing trade, transport links, and investment ties with the West create expansion opportunities. Western banks' claims on borrowers in these regions have risen since 2022.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Switzerland Sign Memoranda of Understanding Worth $46 Million
item.description: Kazakhstan and Switzerland have signed several Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) totaling $46 million. These agreements are expected to foster closer economic ties and cooperation between the two nations. Further details on the specific areas of collaboration were not immediately available.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov Inspects Shymkent's Production and Road Quality
item.description: Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov visited Shymkent to review the city's socio-economic development and the implementation of President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's directives on economic growth and road improvement. He inspected industrial zones, including a tile factory and a transformer manufacturer, and assessed public space development.

item.title: Kazakhstan Overhauls Military Training After Deadly Exercises, Plans New Drone Forces
item.description: Kazakhstan has approved plans to overhaul conscript training and introduce new safeguards against abuse in the armed forces, following a deadly exercise incident. The reform, scheduled for 2027, aims to divide military service into two stages to improve recruit adjustment and reduce hazing. Investigations into the previous tragedy uncovered failures in planning and soldier protection, leading to criminal cases.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Historical Development Path from Declaration to Independence Discussed in Almaty
item.description: A scientific and practical conference was held in Almaty to discuss Kazakhstan's historical development path from the Declaration of State Sovereignty in 1990 to independence. Speakers emphasized the Declaration's significance in laying the foundation for the country's future development and its role as a crucial step towards independence. The event highlighted the importance of understanding history for present and future perspectives.

item.title: Shakhinakhon Yigitalieva Breaks Asian Para Games Record in Javelin Throw
item.description: Shakhinakhon Yigitalieva set a new Asian Para Games record, winning gold in the women's javelin throw (F46) with a distance of 44.99 meters. Khusnorakhon Kudratullaeva secured silver with 41.91 meters. In women's shot put (F35), Dilafruzhon Akhmadkhonova won silver and Zukhro Fayzullaeva bronze. Pokiza Akhmadbekova claimed bronze in cycling.

item.title: Uzbekistan Taekwondo Team Wins Six Medals at Qatar Open Tournament
item.description: Members of the Uzbekistan national taekwondo team secured six medals at the 'Qatar Open' WT tournament in Doha. Yodgorbek Juraboev and Svetlana Saidova won gold medals, Madina Mirabzalova earned silver, and Najmiddin Kosimkhodzhiev, Shabbona Abduvalieva, and Mohidil Uktamzhonova took bronze. Saidova was named 'Best Female Athlete'.

item.title: Kazakhstan Introduces New Performance Metrics for Banks
item.description: Kazakhstan has established new individual performance indicators for all banks concerning customer complaint handling and debt resolution. The Agency for Regulation and Development of the Financial Market announced these measures, which will assess banks on complaint processing quality, reduction of problem loans, and debt restructuring effectiveness. These changes aim to improve customer service and protect borrowers' rights.

item.title: Former Deputy to Build $111 Million Meat Cluster in Turkestan Region
item.description: An agreement has been signed to establish a $111 million meat cluster in the Turkestan region, Kazakhstan. The project, led by Syrym Yertayev, a former Member of Parliament and head of the Meat Union, aims to boost the region's agricultural potential, increase production, and support economic growth. This initiative was part of a larger investment forum where 22 documents totaling $4.8 billion were signed.

item.title: International Network Launched to Support Childhood Cancer Care in Uzbekistan
item.description: An international network aimed at supporting children with serious illnesses, including cancer, has been launched in Samarkand, Uzbekistan. Announced by St. Jude Children's Research Hospital, the initiative will involve first ladies and spouses of heads of state sharing expertise to improve diagnosis, treatment, and access to quality medical care for children globally.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Discusses Nuclear Security Zone and AES Construction
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev met with the head of the Atomic Energy Agency to review 2026 work results. Discussions covered nuclear power plant construction, atomic science development, and establishing a Semipalatinsk nuclear security zone. Special attention was given to improving radioactive waste management and strengthening nuclear safety regulations.

item.title: Kazakhstan Tightens Housing Eligibility Rules, Limits Speculative Applications
item.description: Kazakhstan has revised its preferential housing program rules to prevent individuals with multiple properties from unfairly benefiting. New regulations require applicants' share in their sole residence not to exceed 20%. Previously, a share of up to 50% was permissible. The changes also allow applicants to choose preferred housing districts, addressing previous issues with rejected offers.

item.title: Almaty Luxury Housing Project Faces Criminal Charges and Delays
item.description: The elite Esentai City residential complex in Almaty is embroiled in legal troubles, including criminal cases and construction delays. The project, which began in 2016, has faced issues with communications and unfinished construction. Key figures involved have been convicted of fraud and leading criminal organizations.

item.title: Kazakhstan Expands Middle Corridor Fleet Amid Falling Caspian Sea Levels
item.description: Kazakhstan is expanding its maritime freight capacity by acquiring new vessels to address delays along the Middle Corridor trade route. Falling Caspian Sea levels are complicating port operations and limiting cargo capacity for existing ships, leading to a backlog of containers awaiting shipment.

item.title: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev Reviews Progress in Nuclear Energy Sector
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev met with the Chairman of the Atomic Energy Agency, Almasadam Satkaliev, to review the agency's 2026 performance report. Discussions focused on nuclear power plant construction, atomic science development, workforce training, and increasing local content in industry projects.

item.title: Apple Pay Expected to Launch in Uzbekistan, Following Google Pay
item.description: Uzbekistan anticipates the launch of Apple Pay, enabling contactless smartphone payments for foreign tourists, similar to the existing Google Pay service. Technical work is underway involving the Central Bank, commercial banks, and HUMO and Uzcard systems. Integration with Alipay+ and NPCI International is also progressing to accommodate growing tourist numbers.

item.title: Hundreds of Kazakhs Defrauded in Astana Pyramid Scheme Selling iPhones at Low Prices
item.description: Hundreds of Kazakh citizens were defrauded by the WYP.KZ pyramid scheme in Astana, which promised iPhones and other electronics at below-market prices. The scheme collapsed, leaving victims with losses totaling 216 million tenge. Authorities have shut down six such schemes this year.

item.title: Kazakh President Instructs Development of Nuclear Energy Sector
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev met with Almasadam Satkaliev, Chairman of the Agency for Atomic Energy, and received a report on the sector's development. The President emphasized the importance of building nuclear power plants, advancing nuclear science, and training specialists, instructing that national nuclear energy development be kept under special control.

item.title: OCHA: 8,000 People Gain Access to Safe Drinking Water in Three Afghan Provinces
item.description: The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) announced that 8,000 people in Badakhshan, Baghlan, and Takhar provinces now have access to safe drinking water. The project, supported by the Afghanistan Humanitarian Fund, involved constructing water supply systems. Millions in Afghanistan face water shortages.

item.title: Uzbekistan Recovers $850,000 in Wages for Citizens Working Abroad
item.description: Uzbekistan's Migration Agency has recovered $850,000 in unpaid wages and compensation for 817 citizens working abroad during the first nine months of 2026. The majority of cases involved workers in Russia, followed by Turkey and South Korea. The agency also facilitated the return of identification documents for 532 citizens. Citizens facing difficulties abroad are encouraged to contact the agency.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Targets 8% Annual Economic Growth and Increased FDI Through 2030
item.description: Kyrgyzstan aims for an average annual real GDP growth of at least 8% and a 20% annual increase in foreign direct investment by 2030. The government plans to achieve this by developing export-oriented industries, improving transport routes, and attracting capital. While forecasts suggest growth may exceed 8% this year, sustaining this pace remains a challenge.

item.title: Astana Online Store Owes Customers 216 Million Tenge Amid Fraud Investigation
item.description: An online store in Astana is under investigation for defrauding customers by selling iPhones and other electronics below market value. The company allegedly used funds from new buyers to pay off earlier customers, leading to a debt of 216 million tenge owed to over 200 victims. The investigation is ongoing.

item.title: Tajikistan and South Korea to Enhance Customs Cooperation with Digital Solutions
item.description: Tajikistan plans to improve customs control using new digital solutions supported by South Korea. A key area of cooperation will be developing an automated system for post-customs clearance goods inspection. The initiative aims to detect violations, combat undervaluation, and prevent misclassification of goods, enhancing efficiency and revenue collection.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Allocates Additional 7.6 Billion Som for Social Payment Increases from 2027
item.description: Kyrgyzstan will require an additional 7.6 billion som from the national budget to increase social benefits and monetary compensations starting January 1, 2027. This initiative, proposed by the Ministry of Labor, aims to enhance social protection for various citizen categories, including people with disabilities and veterans.

item.title: Uzbekistan Academy of Sciences to become Asian scientific coordination center
item.description: The Uzbekistan Academy of Sciences has been granted the status and authority to coordinate cooperation with the Asian Academy of Sciences. This decision, made at a forum in China, aims to enhance Uzbekistan's international scientific standing and foster regional research collaboration.

item.title: Tajikistan Considers Raising Pension Age to 63 for Women or 65 for All
item.description: Tajikistan's government is proposing to raise the retirement age. The suggestion is to set it at 63 for women or 65 for everyone. Pensions currently constitute about 22% of wages, and only a third of the working population receives them.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Schools to Receive Starlink High-Speed Internet Access
item.description: Twenty-five Starlink terminals have been provided to schools across Kyrgyzstan to enable high-speed satellite internet access. This initiative aims to bridge the digital divide and ensure equal access to educational resources for students in remote areas. The project, which began as a pilot in 2025, now allows for the permanent use of satellite communication technologies.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Opportunity in the Global Data Center Race
item.description: As global demand for AI computing power surges, Uzbekistan is exploring opportunities to attract major data centers. The country offers a unique combination of special legal regimes, competitive energy tariffs, and renewable energy potential, but needs to attract investors for electricity supply.

item.title: Bishkek Considers Monorail Metro to Alleviate Traffic Congestion
item.description: Bishkek is exploring the possibility of constructing an elevated monorail metro system to address traffic congestion. The initiative, inspired by a visit to a Chinese company, aims to provide fast, convenient, and eco-friendly public transportation.

item.title: Tajikistan Hosts Conference on Geology's Role in Industry and Digitalization
item.description: An international conference on the role of geology in industrial development and the IX Central Asian Micromine-2026 Users Conference are being held in Gulis­ton, Tajikistan. Discussions focus on subsurface exploration, mineral resource assessment, and the impact of digitalization and AI on geological processes. The events commemorate Tajikistan's 35 years of independence.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Registers 49 Polygamy Cases Over Eight Years, Few Reach Conviction
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Prosecutor General's Office reported 49 criminal cases for bigamy and polygamy over eight years, with only five reaching court. Most cases were dismissed due to lack of corpus delicti, and some ended in reconciliation. Experts note that official statistics do not reflect the true scale of polygamy, as many cases remain unreported.

item.title: Khujand Health Centers Conduct Door-to-Door Visits for Disease Prevention
item.description: Health center staff in Khujand, Tajikistan, are conducting door-to-door visits to prevent diseases and identify health issues early. The initiative, ordered by the Health Minister, aims to improve healthcare quality and public awareness of prevention methods. Medical workers assess residents' health, provide health education, and emphasize timely medical attention. These efforts facilitate early problem detection and increase access to medical services.

item.title: Kazakhstan Dominates Flour Imports into Kyrgyzstan, Data Shows
item.description: Kazakhstan holds an almost complete monopoly on flour imports into Kyrgyzstan, supplying over 103,000 tons since the start of the year. Despite a decrease in import value and volume compared to last year, Kazakhstan remains the primary source for Kyrgyzstan's flour needs, which are estimated at around 600,000 tons annually. Russia is a secondary supplier, and some flour is produced domestically from imported grain.

item.title: Iran's Revolutionary Guards Announce Preparation to Unveil 'Father of All Bombs'
item.description: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) spokesperson announced the country is preparing to unveil a new weapon called the 'Father of All Bombs.' While details remain scarce, the IRGC stated it represents a new capability against adversaries and that Iran's missiles have improved in range, destructive power, and accuracy. The announcement follows US President Trump's mention of using the 'Mother of All Bombs' against Iran.

item.title: Kazakhstan Activist Sanzhar Bokaev's Trial: Judge Recusal Denied, Videographer Moved to House Arrest
item.description: In Almaty, lawyers for activist Sanzhar Bokaev, his relative Madiyar Kalmenov, and videographer Ulan Nusipkozha again sought the judge's recusal, which was denied. The court also considered requests to change pre-trial measures. Bokaev and Kalmenov remain in custody, while Nusipkozha is moved to house arrest due to health concerns.

item.title: Over 300 Investors Gather in Bokhtar for 'Khatlon Invest – 2026' Forum
item.description: The international investment forum 'Khatlon Invest – 2026' opened in Bokhtar on October 22, 2026, attracting over 300 domestic and foreign investors. The event featured an exhibition of regional products and investment opportunities. Officials highlighted the region's industrial growth and economic improvements, aiming to attract further investment.

item.title: Kandahar Farmers Face Challenges with Pomegranate Sales Due to Storage and Export Issues
item.description: A Kandahar farmer reports difficulties selling this year's pomegranate harvest due to a lack of storage facilities and limited export options. Periodic border closures with Pakistan exacerbate the problem, leading to potential spoilage. Farmers are requesting access to cold storage and more international markets to reduce losses and recover costs.
